chapters.html:
All Mydei could remember from his childhood was how he always ended up clashing with Phainon.

It was as if they were fated to be born on opposite sides of the world. Mydei came into the palace as a prince, while Phainon began his life as a kid from a small village beyond the kingdom. Everything about them felt like it belonged to different realms, the way the sun stands apart from the moon, chaos from calm, water from fire, the sky from the land.

But even with all those differences the universe placed between them, they still found each other. It was strange in its own quiet way, how something kept pulling them together no matter how far their worlds were meant to stay apart.

They were barely ten when they first crossed paths. It happened on the day the palace opened its outer gates for the midsummer rites, when the villages were allowed to bring their offerings to the capital. 

Mydei slipped away from his caretakers the moment they looked elsewhere, drifting toward the noise in the courtyard where merchants and farmers gathered.

Phainon was there with his village’s procession, carrying a basket that looked heavier than he was. He tried to lift it but stumbled, the basket tipping as fruit scattered across the stone path. The crowd kept moving in a rush, too caught up in the chaos of the procession to even glance at the mess on the ground.

But Mydei noticed, and he moved toward Phainon without hesitation. He dropped to his knees beside him, quietly gathering the fruit and placing each piece back in the basket. Phainon gave him a bright smile and thanked him, but Mydei didn’t say much in return. He simply kept helping until every last piece was back where it belonged.

When the village elder finally noticed the basket, they took it from Phainon and sent him away from the crowd, afraid he’d get knocked over if he stayed. Phainon nodded cheerfully, then spotted Mydei already walking off. He hurried after him and caught his arm, making Mydei yelp at the sudden touch.

“Wait! Come play with me,” Phainon said brightly.

Mydei frowned at him, tilting his head slightly. “There’s no such thing as ‘play’ in my family’s dictionary,” he said. “I’m the crown prince. I’m supposed to train. Not… do that.”

Phainon looked at him for a moment, then grinned like he’d just been handed a challenge.

“Okay,” he said. “Then we won’t call it playing.”

Mydei narrowed his eyes. “Then what?”

Phainon tapped a finger on his chin, thinking for barely a second before snapping his fingers. “Training.”

Mydei scoffed at that. “Training for what?”

“Running,” Phainon said, already bouncing on his feet. “Catching. Dodging. Climbing. All the things a prince needs, right? If you can catch me, you win.”

Before Mydei could argue, Phainon poked his arm and bolted across the courtyard, laughing as he sprinted away.

Mydei stood there, clicked his tongue, and grumbled, “That’s still playing.”

Phainon yelled back, “Nope! We’re training! Come catch me!”

Mydei tried to stay still and remind himself of the real training he was supposed to focus on, his lessons and tutors, and all the rules that had been drilled into him. But Phainon kept darting around, laughing loud enough that even the guards began to glance over.

“Even chickens run faster than you!” Phainon shouted, then burst into laughter again.

That finally made Mydei tighten his grip on himself, and he shouted back, “You’re going to regret comparing me to a chicken!”

Then he ran after Phainon.

The moment he did, Phainon’s grin spread wide across his face, as if he’d finally won the challenge of coaxing Mydei into joining his play.

And as time went on, Mydei never truly stopped playing with him.

Even his mother didn’t mind. As long as he completed his training, she let him slip outside the gates to meet Phainon. She said it was good for him to see life beyond the royal walls and to have a few friends from the village.

And as the years pushed them forward, he kept returning to that same boy. Every spare hour Mydei had was spent chasing Phainon through the fields, climbing old trees, or racing down the dirt roads surrounding the village.

Phainon became a constant in his life, a presence he never managed to shake off. He kept annoying Mydei with endless challenges, yet Mydei could never stay angry for long. 

It was always this strange mix of irritation and anger and the patience he had to keep reminding himself to hold onto, because a crown prince wasn’t supposed to snap at a village kid like Phainon, no matter how much that boy pushed every nerve he had.

He remembered one time when they played heroes behind the storage sheds. There was a wooden sword with blue paint on the hilt, the one every kid wanted because it looked closest to a real knight’s blade. They agreed to settle it with a small bet, something simple like who could climb the old fig tree faster.

Mydei reached for the sword first, certain he had a fair claim, but Phainon slipped in front of him with that quick, infuriating grin. He got the blade first, tapping it against his palm, and said he would only hand it over if Mydei could beat him. Mydei refused, insisting it wasn’t fair for Phainon to hold it before they even started the bet. 

Phainon only laughed and lifted the sword just out of Mydei’s reach. He said he was only making sure Mydei wouldn’t run off with it, so he would be the one to “keep it in watch.”

Hearing that, Mydei felt that familiar spark of irritation, the one Phainon could summon so easily, yet after a quiet grumble he forced himself to swallow it down. Because as a prince, he wasn’t supposed to get into a fight over a painted wooden sword, no matter how much Phainon teased him with it.

Then there was another afternoon by the riverbank where they always explored. They found a smooth, flat stone shaped almost like a shield. Whoever held it would get to lead their little quest, so of course they both reached for it at the exact same time.

Phainon got to it first. He spun around with the stone pressed to his chest and declared it his by “divine discovery,” a phrase he barely understood but loved using because it always annoyed Mydei. When Mydei stepped forward to take it, Phainon backed into the reeds, laughing as he claimed the stone granted him special powers that Mydei “wasn’t noble enough to wield.”

Mydei felt impatience gathering in his throat, that rising frustration he knew all too well. Still, he let out a slow breath and held his ground, because as a prince he wasn’t supposed to shove a village kid into the mud just to take back a stone, even if Phainon was clearly begging for it.

He remembered one morning when they lay under the old willow tree, each of them holding a sheet of paper and a pencil. They were supposed to be drawing heroes and beasts. Mydei was focused on his latest creation, a proud little dragon with stubby wings and a round belly.

Phainon rolled onto his side to look at it, then said it looked exactly like a lopsided potato with legs. Mydei snapped back that it was a dragon, and a strong one at that, but Phainon only laughed and said the potato dragon would probably roll rather than fly across the hill.

And that was the one time Mydei’s patience finally snapped. He lunged forward and bit down on Phainon’s arm, leaving small teeth marks on his skin. Phainon howled, clutching his arm like he’d suffered some terrible injury, then immediately burst into laughter again while Mydei glared at him with all the fury a child could muster.

Which made Phainon grab his paper and start scribbling something quickly.

“Look, it’s you!” he said, pointing proudly at the little face he’d drawn.

( •̀ ᴖ •́ )

“It’s noooot!” Mydei yelled, smacking him repeatedly with his paper while Phainon laughed even harder.

Maybe it was all the time they spent together, or maybe Phainon simply slipped into his thoughts little by little. Whatever the reason was, something in Mydei kept shifting, bit by bit.

He remembered going to his mother after their play, telling her endless stories about the village boy who annoyed him every single day. She always smiled and said Phainon sounded like a fun child to spend time with, that Mydei should keep playing with him.

So he did. And somewhere along the way, they became best friends and rivals all at once.

Time moved on, years sliding past them, and Mydei’s feelings for Phainon kept changing. What started as irritation slowly grew into something else, something he didn’t understand at first. His chest felt strange whenever Phainon laughed or smiled at him, like dozens of butterflies fluttering under his ribs, until he finally realized it had become a crush.

He didn’t realize it was a crush at the beginning. But slowly it became clear. The way he always looked for Phainon in a crowd. The way his chest felt lighter whenever Phainon laughed. The way irritation shifted into something different whenever Phainon leaned in a little too close, as if Mydei’s body understood something long before his mind did. And eventually, he simply accepted it.

And the moment he accepted his feelings, his view of Phainon shifted all at once. Phainon was talking about something simple, something completely forgettable, yet Mydei couldn’t hear a single word. All he saw was the curve of his smile, the way sunlight caught in his hair, and the warmth rising in his own chest. He knew he was in love with the boy who had spent his whole life teasing him, challenging him, and stealing pieces of his heart without ever realizing it.

As they grew older, the feeling settled deeper, and being Phainon’s friend stopped being enough. It crept up on him through the day, the quiet ache of wanting to be something more. 

He tried to keep it buried. He tried to hold on to friendship like it was the safest thing he had. But it hurt to laugh with Phainon and pretend he could keep it to himself. It hurt to stay by his side while keeping his heart locked tight, knowing that one wrong step could destroy everything between them.

And the worst part was how natural it felt to want him every hour of the day. Mydei carried all of it alone, the feelings piling higher and pressing into him harder than he ever expected. Some nights he lay awake wondering how long he could keep hiding it. How long he could stay by Phainon’s side without breaking everything apart. How long he could pretend friendship was enough when his heart kept wanting something more.

One day, in their late teenage years, the annual end-of-year celebration was approaching. It was a day of ceremony and gratitude for the successful harvest, followed by a party at the castle where all the villagers were invited. It was still formal, with everyone expected to wear proper attire, and there would be dancing and all the usual traditions.

“Are you going to the party tonight?” Mydei asked as they sat together under the tree.

Phainon glanced at him. “Of course. I want to enjoy the tasty banquet,” he said brightly.

Mydei hesitated for a moment, thinking about the gossip he’d overheard from the villagers. Then he lowered his voice. “Then… are you going to look for a lady to be your spouse?”

Phainon turned to him, confusion clear on his face. “Hm? Not really. Why?”

“That’s what I’ve been hearing,” Mydei muttered. “Some of the village teens said it’s the kind of event where you go to find a partner.”

Phainon watched him shift, sensing the way Mydei kept glancing over like he was thinking hard about something. Then Phainon’s face lit up, a grin breaking across it. “Ohhh, I get it now.”

Mydei frowned at him. “Get what?”

“You’re worried I’ll find a spouse before you do,” Phainon announced proudly.

“What? No, that’s not—” Mydei tried to argue, but Phainon was already nodding like he’d figured out exactly what Mydei was trying to do.

“It’s alright, Mydei, I’m more interested in the desserts anyway,” Phainon said, patting his shoulder in that teasing way of his. “I’ll wait for your marriage first so you won’t feel lonely. You get lonely fast when I’m not around to bother you. It’s kind of funny how you always get mad, but you still want me there to annoy you.”

He smirked. “Are you developing a strange liking for my teasing or something?”

Mydei stared at him, utterly done. “No, I’m not! And that’s not what I meant.”

“Or,” Phainon continued loudly, still ignoring him, “maybe you’re planning to find someone tonight. Should I warn the girls? Tell them the prince is hunting for a bride?”

“That’s ridiculous.” Mydei clicked his tongue in annoyance.

Phainon laughed and flopped back against the tree. “Relax. I’m kidding. Obviously.”

Mydei let out a slow breath, trying not to raise his voice in response.

“Besides,” Phainon added with a shrug, “me? Finding a spouse? You know I like food more.”

He kicked a pebble, entirely unbothered, and Mydei wondered how someone could be that dense and that charming at the same time.

So Mydei decided, at the very least, that he wanted that dense and oblivious man to look at him differently, even if it was only for one night.

He’d actually had a plan in his mind for weeks, but he never knew when to act on it. Tonight finally felt like the right time

So Mydei walked down the hallway toward his mother’s potion room, the place where she kept all the brews she’d been working on. He checked carefully to make sure she wasn’t inside, listening for any sound of her mixing or muttering over her work. 

Once he was certain the room was empty, he slipped inside to look for the one potion he needed for his plan. He searched through dozens of bottles, picking some up and reading their labels one by one, until he finally found it. The label read “Gender Transformation.”

He held the bottle in his hand for a moment, turning it slowly as he searched for any precautions or extra notes written on the glass. Just as he began to read, the door to the room swung open and his mother stepped inside.

“Oh, Mydei. Are you looking for something here?” his mother asked as she walked toward him with a gentle smile.

But the closer she came, the faster his heart pounded. He swallowed hard and tried his best not to look suspicious.

“I was— uh… I was looking for you. I wanted to ask you something,” he said, gripping the bottle behind him as tightly as he could.

But he should have known better than to think he could fool his mother.

She hummed softly, eyes narrowing with curiosity as she leaned a little to the side. “And what are you holding, my dear?” she asked, trying to peek behind him.

“N—nothing,” he stuttered. “Anyway, Mother, how was your walk today? Did you… uh… find anything interesting on your walk?”

“My walk?” she echoed, amusement creeping into her voice. “My dear, whatever you’re hiding is far more interesting than my stroll through the garden. Are you going to tell your mother what you’re clutching behind your back, hm, Mydeimos?”

As his mother stepped closer to peek behind him, Mydei let out a tiny squeak before blurting, “Mother! Did you see the flowers blooming near the fountain? They were— uh— very beautiful! Like… how can flowers even bloom that blue, right? Amazing!”

His mother narrowed her eyes, noticing the way he kept fidgeting. “The flowers were yellow, Mydei. You saw them with me yesterday.”

Mydei tried to shift the topic again, scrambling for any excuse to send his mother out of the room. “What? No, they couldn’t have been yellow. I… I fear something may be wrong with your sight, Mother. It’s quite serious if you’re unable to see color properly. You should have it checked at once. Right now.”

Instead of stepping away, she just chuckled at his effort. “Mm-hm. I’ll check it after you tell me about the bottle.”

Mydei panicked instantly, shifting the bottle even farther to the side in case his mother caught a glimpse of it. “Bottle? What bottle? I am completely bottle-less. I don’t even— but wait, what is a bottle, Mother? I don’t think that word even has an official definition yet. You should… you should add it to the dictionary in the library immediately.”

“Mydeimos.” She gave him a look that clearly said seriously? before her voice shifted into something more serious. “If the word ‘bottle’ didn’t exist, you wouldn’t be hiding one behind your back like a guilty child. And some of the potions in here are still unstable and need fixing before they can be used. So let me see it first, just in case it’s dangerous.”

Mydei fell silent as his mind scrambled for another excuse, but nothing came. His mother sighed as she gently ushered him aside.

“Fine. I’ll figure it out myself. I keep track of every potion in this room anyway. And since you’re standing right in front of the transformation rack, that means you took something from it. Now let’s see… which potion is missing?” she said as she examined the shelf, pointing at each bottle one by one.

And as she became absorbed in checking the shelves, Mydei suddenly had the idea to slip away while she searched for the missing potion. He quietly moved a step back, hoping he could leave before she noticed anything.

But the moment he moved, she put her hand on her hip and glared at him. “Mydeimos. Don’t even think about it.”

Mydei sighed and stood perfectly still as she read out the potions one by one.

“Alright, let’s see… this one turns you into a shrimp, this one into a statue… uhm, this one’s a frog, this one’s a fish…”

She paused, eyes narrowing at the next empty slot.

“Hmm… this one is missing, and it turns you into—OH!” she yelped.

Then her eyes widened, and a slow smirk spread across her face as she turned toward him.

“Oh Mydeii~” she sang. “Who’s the lucky gentleman?”

And suddenly the room felt far too hot for him. He could feel his whole face turning red from the temperature, yes definitely the temperature, not for any other reason. “W–What nonsense are you talking about, Mother… I—I don’t even…”

“As you want to turn yourself into a pretty princess, which prince has captured your heart, hm?” his mother said. “Is it… the boy you keep talking about all the time? Phainon, was it?” She stepped closer, trying to catch his eyes as he desperately avoided her gaze.

Mydei finally sighed, realizing there was no point in lying anymore. There was never any fooling his all-knowing mother.

“Fine… yes.” He lowered his gaze. “It’s just… I want to be able to try flirting with him openly, even for one night, as someone else. I can’t do it as… me.”

“And why can’t you do it as yourself?” his mother asked gently.

Mydei’s shoulders sank. “Because we’ve been friends our whole lives… and I’m scared,” he admitted. “If he doesn’t feel the same, he might end our friendship. I don’t want to lose him.”

He finally held out the little bottle to her, his fingers trembling just a bit.

His mother took the bottle from his hand and turned it over slowly, studying the label before looking back at him.

“Mydei… you don’t need a potion to make someone love you,” she said softly. “But you do need courage to tell them how you feel.”

Mydei looked away, realizing how foolish his plan sounded now that his mother had pointed it out. “I know… but I don’t have that courage yet.”

She reached out and cupped his cheek, guiding his eyes back to hers. “You are my son. You have more courage than you realize.”

Then she tapped the bottle lightly. “But if you insist on trying this, at least let me make sure it’s safe. I’m not letting you turn yourself into a frog by accident.”

Mydei let out a weak laugh. “Please don’t let me turn into a frog…”

“I won’t,” she promised with a smile. “Now tell me exactly what you’re planning for this boy of yours.”

Mydei’s heart beat faster, but he took a breath and explained that tonight, at the party, he wanted to ask Phainon for a dance and try to flirt with him openly, just to see how he reacted. Maybe get close enough to understand if there was even a chance for him. And if the moment felt right… he wanted to tell him how he truly felt.

His mother listened quietly, her expression softening as the pieces of his plan came together. She held the little bottle between her fingers, turning it once before letting out a thoughtful hum.

“Mydei, love doesn’t need disguises.” Then she added, with a gentle smile, “But if this is the only way you can find your courage, I will help you do it safely.”

Relief washed over him so suddenly his knees felt weak.”Thank you, Mother,” he whispered.

“Now,” she said, lifting the bottle up to the light, “let me prepare this properly. I won’t have you turning into a half-human half-insect by accident.”

Mydei let out a strangled noise.”Mother, please don’t joke about that.”

She only laughed softly. “Go get ready for the celebration, my son. I’ll bring this to you once it’s safe to drink.”

Mydei had just finished his bath and was still in his robe when his mother stepped into his room. She carried several bags with her, practically glowing with excitement as she walked up to him.

He was rubbing a towel through his wet hair when she reached him.

“Mydeimos, your mother has finally perfected the potion for you,” she sang. “And I brought some pretty dresses for you to try too. Oh my gods, I’m actually so excited!” she shrieked happily.

She set the bags on his bed and pulled something from her pocket.

“Here,” she said, handing him the bottle, which was noticeably smaller now. “You can drink this safely. And since you only need it for tonight, I measured it so the effect ends around three in the morning. It took a while, but it is done. And you are not allowed to stay with him until morning. In case of an unplanned pregnancy.”

Mydei stared at her, completely confused as he looked at the tiny bottle. “Huh? I do not understand how pregnancy is involved in any of this.”

His mother simply chuckled. “I am joking. Just drink it.”

Mydei shrugged, lifted the bottle, and took a sip. It tasted surprisingly decent, a faint sweetness lingering on his tongue, so he just drank the rest in one go.

When he finished, he stood there quietly. He and his mother both waited, staring at him, expecting something to happen… but nothing did.

“Huh?” Mydei muttered, glancing back at the empty bottle.

“How is it?” his mother asked, watching him closely.

“I don’t really feel anything yet, Mother,” he said, though his voice suddenly sounded higher than before. “W… wait.”

Mydei suddenly felt himself shrinking, his robe growing larger around him. A weight formed on his chest as two soft lumps grew fuller, shifting his balance. His hair lengthened too, brushing against his back, longer than it had ever been.

His eyes widened just as the robe slipped off his shoulders and fell to the floor in a heap.

He yelped and scrambled to cover himself, one arm pressed across his chest while he crossed his legs and used his free hand to shield his lower half.

“Oh dear, how indecent,” his mother chuckled.

“D… don’t laugh, Mother, help me,” Mydei said, completely mortified.

His mother walked over to the bags she had brought and pulled out a few items.

“Alright, here is a corset and the underwear you should wear,” she said as she passed them to him.

Mydei stayed frozen in his awkward position, staring at the corset like it had come from another planet. “Uhm… how do I even wear this? Why does it have strings and so many holes?”

His mother smiled and handed him the underwear. “Alright, this first. Then I’ll teach you how to put on the rest.”

Mydei looked down at the fabric, then back at her. “Okay… but can you slip it onto my arm here and then turn around while I put it on?”

His mother laughed softly. “Why are you so shy, my dear? Fine, I’m turning around.”

She turned her back to him, humming softly as she waited. Mydei quickly slipped on the underwear, still trying to cover himself with one arm across his chest as best he could.

“Mother… I’m done,” he said quietly.

She turned around with a bright smile and lifted the corset. “Good. Now arms up.”

Mydei raised his arms, and she slipped the corset around his waist, adjusting the fabric and tying the strings carefully. He winced as she tugged it a bit tighter.

“Is it supposed to feel like I’m being squeezed?” he asked.

“That means it’s working,” she said cheerfully as she tightened another string. “Beauty takes effort, my dear.”

Mydei groaned under his breath but let her continue, watching his new body take form little by little under her hands. 

When she finished adjusting the corset and finally stepped back, she gave him an approving nod.

“There. Beautiful,” she said, brushing a few loose strands of his longer hair behind his shoulder. “Now for the dress.”

She reached for one of the bags and pulled out a dress made of soft red fabric that shimmered slightly in the light. She twirled it happily in her hands.

“A beautiful dress for the most beautiful princess,” she said with delight.

“I’m not a princess,” Mydei muttered, feeling his cheeks warm up.

“Aww, but you look very pretty, my dear,” she said as she lifted the dress. “Now lift your arms again.”

He obeyed, and she slipped the dress over his head, guiding the fabric down carefully so it settled over his corseted waist and hips. The hem brushed against his ankles.

His mother stepped around him, adjusting the folds, smoothing the skirt, and tying a small ribbon behind him.

“There. You look lovely, Mydei.”

He stared down at himself, then muttered, “It feels so strange.”

“You’ll get used to it,” she said warmly. “Now sit. I need to fix your hair.”

Mydei sat on the stool she pulled closer, smoothing the skirt awkwardly as he tried not to step on it. His mother stood behind him and gathered his long hair gently, combing through the strands that hadn’t even existed an hour ago.

“You have such nice hair like this,” she said as she worked. “So soft and thick. It suits you.”

Mydei watched her in the mirror, feeling more embarrassed with each passing minute.

“It feels too long. It keeps touching my back.”

“That is what long hair does, my dear,” she laughed softly as she twisted a small section and pinned it neatly. “But it frames your face beautifully.”

When she finished pinning the last strand, his mother placed her hands on his shoulders.

“There. Now for your makeup,” she said brightly, reaching into one of the bags to pull out a small box.

And if he already felt embarrassed before, he couldn’t believe it could actually get worse once his mother leaned in close, her face only inches from his as she worked with tiny brushes and powders.

Mydei kept scrunching his nose and tightening his mouth every time the brush touched his skin, which only made things harder.

“Mydeimos, relax your face,” his mother scolded gently, tapping his chin. “I cannot do this if you keep wrinkling everything.”

He tried, he really did, but every sweep of the brush made him tense up again.

He forced himself to sit still for the rest of it, even though every part of him hoped his mother wouldn’t pull out any more mysterious tools he didn’t recognize.

Finally, she dabbed a bit of color on his cheeks and lifted his chin with a satisfied hum.

“There. Pretty,” she said. “You already have such delicate features and such a lovely face. Well, of course you do, it comes from your pretty mother.” She flicked her hair proudly. “A little makeup is more than enough.”

Mydei stared at his reflection, feeling his face heat even more. Everything about him looked different now. Softer. Smaller. Beautiful in a way he had never seen in himself before.

“I look… too different,” he murmured.

His mother only smiled and patted his shoulder. “That is exactly what you wanted, isn’t it? For him to see someone new tonight.”

Mydei swallowed, unsure if he was ready for that reality.

She stepped back and clapped her hands together. “Alright. The last thing you need is your shoes.”

She reached into one of the bags and pulled out a pair of delicate heels that sparkled faintly under the light.

Mydei’s face went pale. “Mother. Those look dangerous.”

“No, it is not,” she said firmly as she knelt down. “Now, foot up.”

Reluctantly, he lifted his foot, and she slipped the heels on. They fit perfectly, but he wasn’t sure at all if he could actually walk in them.

“There,” she said with delight. “Now try to stand.”

He stood slowly, wobbling the moment he put weight on them.

“I am going to fall and die before the party even starts,” Mydei whispered in horror.

His mother steadied him with both hands, holding his arms until he found some balance. “You are being dramatic,” she said lightly. “Take a few steps. Slowly.”

Mydei shook his head. “I can barely stand. Walking sounds like a death wish.”

“Try,” she encouraged, giving him a gentle nudge.

He took one careful step.

Then another.

On the third, his ankle tilted and he flailed, grabbing onto her shoulders for dear life.

“See? I told you! I don’t think I can do this. Can I please use flat shoes or something?”

She laughed softly and helped him straighten up again.

“You’ll manage at the party. Just keep your steps small and find your balance. And if you feel unsteady, hold on to Phainon.” She gave him a playful wink.

Mydei’s face turned bright red. “Mother, please.”

“What? That is what he is for tonight,” she teased. “Your handsome support.”

He groaned and covered his face with both hands.

“Alright, quit the whining and go to the hall first. I need to prepare now,” she said, shooing him gently toward the door.

Mydei followed behind her, still wobbling, still flailing a little, but starting to find his balance. After a bit of quiet arguing with himself, he decided he would master these shoes tonight. At the very least, he wanted to not embarrass himself in front of Phainon.

As they walked down the hallway, they ran into his father coming from the opposite direction. He stopped. Mydei stopped. They both just stared at each other in complete silence.

His mother cleared her throat and broke into a bright smile. “See? He’s taking after me more!”

His father only clicked his tongue in disappointment before walking past them without another word.

Mydei didn’t react and only sighed. As he grew older, he had long understood his father’s disappointment in everything he did. Being ignored like that was something he had already grown used to.

He walked his mother to her room, thanked her for helping him, and then headed toward the party hall on the first floor. If walking on heels across flat ground was already a challenge, going down the stairs was an entirely new nightmare. He clung to the railing for dear life, taking each step like it might be his last.

Fortunately, the stairs weren’t located in the main hall, so he didn’t have to humiliate himself in front of the guests. But even then, a few guards spotted him wobbling and rushed toward him in a panic, unsure whether to catch him or give him space.

It was utterly mortifying.

But finally, he managed to join the crowd already gathered in the hall. Some people were dancing in the center, others stood near the banquet tables chatting with one another. Mydei slipped into the flow of the room, trying to look composed as he scanned the crowd, searching for Phainon.

Usually, during parties like this in the castle, he would already be surrounded by guests since he was the crown prince. But with this disguise, people only glanced at him before moving on, leaving him completely alone.

He looked around for a while, politely declining a few men who had already approached to ask him for a dance. He kept searching until he finally spotted Phainon at the dessert table, happily piling sweets onto his plate.

And when their eyes met, Mydei gave him a small smile. Phainon frowned in confusion, then lifted a finger and pointed to himself as if asking, “Who? Me?”

Mydei wanted to punch that stupid face for making such a ridiculous expression, but he swallowed it down and started walking toward him instead. Phainon watched as he approached, confusion written all over him, and slowly set his plate down on the table.

“You look very beautiful tonight, Myde— I mean, my lady,” Phainon said as Mydei stopped in front of him.

Mydei narrowed his eyes on him immediately.

Assuming it was just Phainon being Phainon, he let the irritation go and stepped closer with as much grace as he could manage. He lifted his hand and rested it lightly on Phainon’s arm, his fingers brushing along the fabric up to his shoulder. 

Mydei moved in closer, looping his arm around Phainon’s shoulder and letting their chests press gently together.

Phainon yelped at the sudden closeness. “Wh-what—?” he blurted, eyes wide in pure confusion.

“May I have this dance?” Mydei asked softly as he leaned in closer, their breaths mingling between them.

“Sure…” Phainon whispered, his eyes flicking toward Mydei with a noticeable shift, as if something in his gaze had changed. Mydei felt Phainon’s hand settle on his waist, his thumb brushing gently along his side.

And for a moment, Mydei wondered who was actually flirting with who now.

Phainon led him toward the center of the hall, and Mydei tried his absolute best to move with him. But the heels betrayed him at every step, making him stumble more than he actually danced.

Mydei lowered his head and cursed quietly at himself, which made Phainon chuckle. Then Phainon leaned in close to Mydei’s ear and whispered, “You are awful at dancing, princess.”

Mydei shot him a sideways glare, trying not to trip over his own feet again.

“Oh, thank you,” he muttered. “What a gentleman you are.”

Phainon laughed under his breath as he slipped a hand to Mydei’s waist, supporting his movements. With his other hand, he gently guided Mydei’s arm to loop over his shoulder.

“I’m only telling the truth,” he said, giving him a gentle smile.

“Then perhaps you should try dancing in these heels,” Mydei snapped softly, still forcing himself to keep moving. “Let’s see how graceful you are.”

Phainon raised a brow, clearly amused. “Is that a challenge, princess?”

Mydei narrowed his eyes on him. “It’s a warning,” he muttered. “Insult me one more time and I’ll step on you.”

Phainon chuckled, tightening his hand on Mydei’s waist just enough to steady him. “Wouldn’t be the first time you tried to step on me.”

“So annoying,” Mydei hissed, stumbling slightly as his heel wobbled.

Phainon caught him instantly, pulling him closer before he could fall.

Their chests brushed, close enough that Mydei could feel Phainon’s breath warm against his cheek.

“Careful,” Phainon murmured. “I’d hate to drop you.”

Mydei’s heart skipped faster as heat crawled up his neck. “Just… stop talking and focus on the dance,” he whispered back.

Phainon’s smile widened. “If you say so, princess.”

They moved with the rhythm as Phainon guided him, and Mydei’s steps slowly matched the pace. Music swelled around them, filling the hall with warmth and laughter, blurring the rest of the crowd until it felt like there were only the two of them.

But from the corner of his eye, Mydei caught sight of his mother on the high podium. The moment their eyes met, she lifted her hand and gave him an enthusiastic thumbs-up.

Embarrassment hit him hard. His cheeks grew warmer and warmer, and he panicked enough to drop his head against Phainon’s chest to hide his face.

“Hm? What’s wrong?” Phainon asked softly as they kept moving through the dance.

“Nothing,” Mydei muttered into his chest. “I just… feel like I need some fresh air.”

Phainon slowed their steps and dipped his head a little, trying to see Mydei’s face.

“Do you want to step outside?” he asked softly.

Mydei nodded without lifting his head. “Just for a moment.”

Hearing that, Phainon guided him toward the edge of the hall, moving carefully so Mydei wouldn’t stumble again. They slipped out into the quiet garden outside, the cool air brushing against Mydei’s flushed skin.

Only then did he finally lift his head, looking at Phainon, who gave him a big smile.

Flustered, he tried to step back, but Phainon’s hand slipped around his waist and held him in place. The grip tightened just enough to pull him closer, closing the space Mydei desperately needed. Phainon’s other hand rose to Mydei’s chin, guiding his face back up toward him.

“I believe our dance isn’t over yet, princess,” he murmured with a smirk.

Mydei’s eyes widened at the sudden shift in Phainon’s behavior, but then he remembered why he was doing all of this in the first place. He wasn’t here to get teased by him. He was here to flirt openly and finally say what he’d been holding inside for years.

So he gathered what little courage he had left. He slipped his arms back around Phainon, leaned in slowly, and pressed a soft kiss to his lips.

He felt Phainon’s body jolt at the sudden kiss, a brief stiffening that told Mydei he’d caught him completely off-guard. But when Mydei nipped softly at his bottom lip and let his tongue brush against it, Phainon let out a quiet hum and leaned in without hesitation, returning the kiss.

The moment he responded, their kiss deepened. Mydei tightened his arms around Phainon’s shoulders, pulling him closer, while Phainon’s grip on his waist tightened in return, strong enough to draw him in until there was no space left between them.

When they finally broke apart for air, Phainon didn’t pull away. He stayed close, his forehead resting lightly against Mydei’s, his breath still brushing across Mydei’s lips.

“I’ve never seen you this bold when we meet normally…” Phainon whispered, his smirk growing. “Got something you’ve been holding back, Mydei?”

Mydei’s eyes narrowed at him. “You knew from the beginning, didn’t you? You just teased me on purpose.”

Phainon suddenly burst into laughter. “Of course I’d know it’s you. Even if you transformed into a rock, I’d still know.”

“Tsk.” Mydei clicked his tongue in annoyance.

Phainon watched him with open amusement.

“I must say, you look very beautiful as a lady. All this dress and everything… is it for me? I’m very thankful. Aww, do you like me that much? I still like the usual Mydei better, though. Don’t get me wrong—yes, you’re pretty now, but you’re still pretty as—”

As Phainon kept rambling, words piling over each other, Mydei finally had enough. He leaned in and pressed his lips to Phainon’s again, just enough to shut him up. When he pulled back, he glared right at him.

“Listen here, Phainon.” He took a breath before continuing. “You better listen closely, because there’s something I’ve been keeping to myself for a long time. But I don’t think I can talk about it as myself… because our friendship—”

Before he could finish, Phainon cut him off.

“Then I don’t want to hear it,” he said simply.

Mydei stared at him, stunned, and managed a quiet, “What?”

Phainon’s expression softened as he took Mydei’s hand in his.

“You need to say your feelings as you. If you think this isn’t you, then I don’t want to hear it.”

“No, there will be no other chance, so you better listen or—” Mydei pressed his finger against Phainon’s chest to emphasize every word.

“I don’t wanna— la la la—” Phainon said immediately, cutting him off as he turned away, covering his ears with both hands while walking in the opposite direction.

Mydei clenched his fists and stormed after him. “Phainon!” he yelled.

But as soon as he got close, his heel wobbled and he stumbled forward.

“Whoa, careful there.” Phainon caught him at once, steadying him with both hands. Mydei clung to his arm, still glaring up at him despite nearly falling flat on his face.

Mydei sighed and took a deep breath, trying to calm himself. “Are you going to listen to me now?” he asked.

Phainon only smiled at him. “Why are you so frustrated over this?” he said softly. “Are you scared it’ll ruin our friendship?”

Before Mydei could snap back, Phainon slid his hands to Mydei’s waist again, pulling him closer. Then he pressed soft kisses across Mydei’s cheeks, his forehead, the tip of his nose before settling on his lips.

When he finally pulled back, he held Mydei close and looked straight into his eyes.

“Tell me tomorrow,” he murmured.

“And if you’re still unsure… I’ll give you one hint.” His thumb brushed Mydei’s cheek. “My feelings are exactly what you’ve already seen from how I treated you tonight.”

Hearing that didn’t help Mydei at all. It gave him no answer, no clarity, not even the slightest hint of what Phainon truly felt. All night Phainon had treated him the same way he always did, and it left Mydei even more frustrated than before.

Knowing he wouldn’t get anything useful out of him tonight, and unable to say anything more about what he felt, Mydei shot him one last glare before turning and marching back toward the castle.

“Wait, princess,” Phainon called from behind him.

Mydei turned toward him, still bristling.

Phainon pointed at the ground with a grin.

“You forgot to leave one of your shoes for me.”

Mydei rolled his eyes at him, then leaned down to pull off his heels. Without a second thought, he hurled them at Phainon as hard as he could.

One heel struck Phainon right in the face and the other hit his chest. He let out a soft “Ouch—” then lifted a thumb up.

Mydei turned without looking back and headed inside barefoot, which honestly felt far better than wearing those heels anyway.

Walking back to his room, his mood completely ruined, Mydei muttered angrily the whole way, “Dumb Phainon… how can someone be this dumb… I hate him so much.”

When Mydei finally reached his bedroom door and pushed it open, he let out a long sigh. He dropped face-first onto his bed and lay there with his eyes shut, already regretting every life choice that had led him to this moment, especially everything he’d done tonight.

He groaned into his pillow, kicking his feet weakly against the mattress like a child throwing a tantrum.

“Why did I even think of this stupid plan… why did I do all of this…” he mumbled, each complaint muffled by the pillow.

Mydei rolled onto his back and stared up at the ceiling.

“He didn’t even take me seriously. He never takes me seriously. He probably thinks this is another joke,” he muttered.

He covered his face with both hands, the regret washing over him all over again. “I’d rather confess to a wall than to that stupid man.”

After lying on his bed for a while, drowning in regret, the quiet of his room broke when his door suddenly opened.

“Mydei?” his mother’s soft voice called out.

She spotted him sprawled on the bed and immediately frowned. She walked over and sat beside him.

“Why are you back already? How was it, hm?”

He shifted closer and rested his head on his mother’s lap, looping his arms weakly around her waist.

“Mother…” he muttered, sounding so miserable.

As if she could sense the storm brewing inside him, she immediately deployed the one weapon only mothers possess. Her hand slid into his still-long hair, stroking gently, her voice softening to something almost magical.

“Hey, it’s alright… What did he do to you, hm? Want to tell your mother?”

It was the oldest trick in the book, the one ultimate technique only mothers had. Even the strongest soldier would melt the moment a mother started rubbing their hair like that. And Mydei was no exception. His frustration cracked at the edges, his body sinking into her lap as he began to sniffle against her.

“He… he… ughh—” he choked, the words breaking apart as tears clogged his throat.

“Shh, it’s alright…” his mother murmured, rubbing his hair even softer.

Her gentle strokes only drew more tears from him, slipping out faster than he could stop them.

“He… made fun of me,” Mydei finally managed to say, melting even deeper into her lap.

Before his mother could respond, his bedroom door slammed open with a bang.

“WHO DARES TO MAKE FUN OF THE PRINCESS!” his father roared from the doorway, his voice echoing down the hall.

The shout startled even his mother, and Mydei lifted his head just enough to stare at him in disbelief.

His father turned back toward the hall and bellowed, loud enough for the entire castle to hear,

“SOLDIERS! TRACK DOWN THE SCOUNDREL WHO INSULTED THE CROWN PRINCESS… PRINCE! BRING ME HIS HEAD BY SUNRISE!”

Mydei only grew more upset, and he pleaded softly,

“Mother, can you please tell Father not to hunt Phainon down?”

But his mother frowned, crossing her arms.

“He deserves to be hunted. No one insults my son.”

“No… it was just the friend kind of teasing,” Mydei muttered. “He didn’t actually insult me…”

His mother looked at him for a long moment, then let out a soft sigh. 

“Are you sure about that?”

Mydei blinked up at her and said weakly, “Yes. I don’t want this to become bigger than it needs to be.”

She hummed in reply, her hand returning to his hair in a soothing stroke.

“Alright. If that’s what you want, I’ll talk to your father,” she murmured. “Though the chances of him actually listening are very slim. You know how he is.”

Mydei groaned into her lap.

“I know.”

After his mother left, Mydei lay on the bed for a while before finally dragging himself up to shower and change. After bathing, he slipped into his usual clothes, which hung loosely on his smaller form. He knew he would return to normal around three in the morning anyway, so he didn’t bother adjusting anything.

A sudden knock at the door interrupted his thoughts.

Mydei got up and opened it, finding one of the servants standing there, looking completely panicked.

“Your Highness,” the servant said breathlessly, “you need to come to the audience hall immediately.”

Feeling certain it had something to do with Phainon, Mydei hurried ahead without another word.

When he arrived at the hall, Mydei froze where he stood, a quiet gasp escaping him at the sight before him.

Right in front of his father’s throne, Phainon was forced onto his knees like a criminal, his hands tied behind his back. Two guards stood behind him, their swords crossed at his neck. Phainon’s head hung low, his hair a complete mess.

His father towered over him, voice booming through the room.

“Tell me what you said to him! And don’t even think about lying to my face.”

Phainon finally lifted his head to look at the king, and he didn’t even look scared. If anything, he just looked tired.

“Your Majesty, I already told you,” he said. “I didn’t say anything worth dragging me here for.”

Mydei rushed forward to Phainon’s side and immediately barked an order for the guards to step back from him.

The guards hesitated at first, glancing between Mydei and the king. But Mydei’s voice came out angrier than they had ever heard it.

“I said move away from him!”

They obeyed immediately. The blades lifted from Phainon’s neck, and the guards stepped aside.

Mydei dropped to his knees beside Phainon, quickly checking him for any bruises or cuts.

“Are you hurt?”

Phainon looked up at him with that same bright, ridiculous grin he always wore.

“Oh, Mydei, I’m perfectly fine. As you can see, I’m just relaxing here,” he said as if he weren’t tied up like a sacrifice.

Mydei huffed under his breath and worked quickly to untie his hands, then guided him to his feet.

As soon as Phainon was on his feet, Mydei turned to face his father, anger simmering beneath his exhaustion.

“Father,” he said in a pressed voice, “Phainon didn’t do anything wrong.”

His father’s brows drew together. “He insulted you. And if you aren’t brave enough to face him, then I will show you how someone who dares insult royalty should be treated.”

Mydei clenched his jaw. “No. He didn’t. He just—” He stopped, heat rising in his cheeks. “it doesn’t matter. He didn’t insult me.”

When his father tried to snap back at him, Mydei only rolled his eyes. He grabbed Phainon’s hand, gripping it tightly as he pulled him away.

“Let’s go,” he muttered. “You didn’t deserve to be dragged into this ridiculousness.”

But Phainon stopped him, slipping an arm around his waist and brushing a hand gently against Mydei’s cheek.

“Why are your eyes swollen?” he asked softly. “Have you been crying, Mydei?”

Mydei tried to turn his face away, but Phainon caught his chin and held him still, forcing their eyes to meet.

“I–It’s not important,” Mydei muttered, embarrassment rushing up all at once. “Let’s go. I’ll walk you home.”

“It is important,” Phainon said softly, leaning in closer. “Seeing you this upset… Did something I said make you sad?”

“No—nothing,” Mydei muttered quickly, his nerves spiking as he felt the eyes of everyone around them still watching. He wanted to disappear on the spot.

“Really? Because it hurts me too to imagine you being sad,” Phainon said, still inching closer like he had no awareness of the dozens of eyes on them.

“I’m fine now, don’t get overdramatic,” Mydei muttered, trying to pull away, only for Phainon to tighten his grip on him.

“Is my hint not enough, my love?” Phainon tilted his head and gave him those wide, pathetic puppy eyes of his.

Mydei yelped on the spot, now trying to get away from him even more.

“Wait—wait, I’m okay, it’s okay, I’m really fine now,” Mydei said in a panic, hands flailing a little as he tried to pull away from Phainon’s grip.

Phainon only smiled at him and simply said, “I’m glad.”

And before Mydei could even breathe, Phainon leaned in and captured his lips.

Mydei jolted, eyes going wide. Phainon didn’t just land a quick peck on his lips. He stayed there longer, even nibbling at his lower lip shamelessly. Mydei could hear the collective gasp rising through the hall around them.

Mortified, he shoved both hands against Phainon’s chest, pushing him back before he completely died of embarrassment.

“Enough! Guards, drag him outside!” Mydei’s father suddenly roared.

The guards finally stepped forward, grabbing Phainon by the shoulders and hauling him across the hall toward the front doors.

And even then, Phainon still somehow found a way to be annoying.

He twisted in their grip and shouted down the hall,

“I’ll see you tomorrow, my princess! Dream of me tonight! Let us meet in your sweet dreams— remember our loooove!”

His voice echoed along the hall’s walls even as he was dragged outside.

Never in his life had Mydei wished harder for the floor to open up and swallow him whole.

There was something deep in him that refused to face Phainon this morning. The embarrassment from last night sat heavy in his chest, so heavy he could barely believe he’d managed to wake up at all. 

He had been having a perfectly normal dream until the moment he opened his eyes and remembered every single thing he had done yesterday.

And after taking far too long to drag himself toward their usual spot, he finally saw Phainon from a distance. He was already there, relaxing under the tree with his gaze fixed on the sky through the leaves. A small wheat stem rested between his lips, which he chewed on lazily while he lay back against the sun-warmed rock.

Mydei sighed, straightened himself, and walked over to him. When he stopped beside the rock, Phainon gave him a brief glance before turning his eyes back to the sky.

Mydei lowered himself beside him, settling quietly at his side.

After a while, Phainon finally started talking. 

“So, something strange happened to me last night at the ceremony… it all happened so fast it felt like a fever dream,” he said with a soft chuckle.

“Anyway, like I told you before, I went to the party for the desserts. I even grabbed two plates because I was getting some for my dear friend too, but he didn’t even show up.”

Mydei stayed quiet, letting him ramble on.

“So there I was, minding my own business, when I saw this really pretty lady. And she noticed me too. She smiled, and I was like… wait, that sweet smile was for me? Then she started walking toward me, and I panicked because I didn’t even go there to dance. I went to challenge my friend to a dessert eating battle. But she was so fine and so flirty that I thought… okay, why not dance with her even though I was still waiting for my dear friend?”

He kept going, not even glancing at Mydei.

“So we danced. She was pretty, but her dancing wasn’t pretty at all. She kept stumbling, but she was cute about it, getting all flustered and blushy when I told her how terrible she was. And she reminded me a lot of this friend I adore. Same glare, same tone, even the same hair. But with her… maybe I had a chance to talk about my feelings. I felt braver flirting with her, because she reminded me so much of the person I actually like.”

He sighed. “But then I thought about it and realized my friend wouldn’t flirt like that in public. He’s not that brave, even if he keeps claiming he’s fearless enough to fight off bandits. No matter how much I wish he actually was.”

“Then she asked to go outside, so I helped her to the garden. And the whole time, I was trying to feel brave… just for that one night… pretending it was him instead of her. So when she leaned in for a kiss, I kissed her back, thinking it would stay as a one-night thing.”

His voice softened. “But then I got sad. Because that was the moment I realized I was being a coward. Even if I had her beside me for one night, I still wanted the real thing… but I didn’t have the courage, so I just played pretend. Call me greedy, but I wanted our feelings to be real, not something that disappears after one night. So I told her to keep whatever she wanted to tell me to herself, because she wasn’t even real.”

Mydei picked up a small stick lying beside him and started absently scribbling circles into the dirt as he listened.

“And as soon as I said that,” Phainon continued with a laugh, “she threw her heels at me.” He shifted, grabbing a small box beside him. He opened it and held it out for Mydei to see the very same pair of heels he’d worn the night before.

“You can keep them,” Mydei muttered, grumbling under his breath.

“What? Why would I keep them? I can’t even wear those,” Phainon laughed, louder this time. “Besides, I don’t want your mother hunting me down next for stealing her shoes.”

“Fine, I’ll take them to my mother later,” Mydei muttered, sliding the box to his other side.

Phainon snorted. “You should’ve seen my parents’ faces when the royal guards showed up at our door last night. They were horrified, thinking their lovely, very kind, and very innocent son had committed some terrible crime.” He chuckled at the memory.

“I’m truly sorry about that,” Mydei murmured, his shoulders sinking. “I didn’t think my father would react like that…”

Phainon nudged him lightly with his elbow. “Hey. Don’t look so guilty. I survived, didn’t I? That was nothing.” He lifted his hands, showing the faint rope marks with a grin. “See? Perfectly fine.”

Mydei frowned at the marks anyway, his voice softening. “Still… I’m sorry.”

Phainon tilted his head, studying him for a moment before a slow smile spread across his face.

“Well, that was my side of the story,” he said lightly. “Now I want to hear yours.”

Mydei looked at him, then reached for the little stick again and went back to scribbling lines into the dirt.

“My story…” he began softly. “I don’t really know when I started having feelings for you. There’s no exact moment I can point to. It was just… growing. Little by little.”

He drew another line in the dirt, watching it instead of Phainon.

“All this time, as I grew up, my head was always filled with thoughts of this annoying friend of mine who lived outside the castle walls. The one I kept playing with every chance I got.” He let out a small laugh. “It doesn’t mean I didn’t care about our other friends. But with you… it was always different.”

He took a slow breath. “It was the way I kept looking for you in crowds. The way I waited for you to come back from helping your parents in the wheat fields so we could play again. Somehow, without me noticing, those little things turned into something more.”

The stick slipped from his fingers, falling onto the ground. Mydei pulled his knees up and wrapped his arms around them.

“And because I thought you saw me as just a friend, I kept it all to myself,” he whispered. “I didn’t want to ruin anything.”

Mydei rested his chin on his knees. “Then one day… this plan just slipped into my head. I wanted to do something to make you see me as something more. I wanted to know how you would act around someone you adored. I wanted to see how you’d treat them. I wanted to know everything, because I got greedy.”

He closed his eyes as a light breeze brushed through his hair.

“So I thought… if I could disguise myself and seduce you for just one night, you wouldn’t know it was me. And maybe… I could finally fill that curiosity I’ve had for so long.”

“And did it fill your curiosity?” Phainon asked, turning fully toward him now with that familiar amused tilt of his head.

Mydei let out a small, embarrassed laugh. “I didn’t expect you’d treat me the same way you always do.”

“That’s right. It’s because I’ve always adored you,” Phainon said brightly.

Mydei snorted at that, feeling his face heat up even more. Phainon just grinned and reached for his hand, fingers slipping between his as he scooted closer. With a little wiggle, he settled right beside him and rested his head on Mydei’s shoulder.

“…Idiot. You made me worry, being all vague last night,” Mydei muttered under his breath, though there was no real bite in it.

“Hm? Is that why you cried?” Phainon asked, turning his head to look at him.

When he saw Mydei’s cheeks slowly growing red, he chuckled and leaned in to give him a quick peck.

“No. I cried because my mother started brushing my hair,” Mydei muttered, shooting him a side glare.

“Ah, yeah… I get that,” Phainon laughed. “I start crying too whenever my mother suddenly hugs me and tells me she’s proud of me.”

“Speaking of your mother… I feel like I should properly apologize to your parents,” Mydei said quietly. “After what the royal guards did last night.”

Phainon suddenly sat up, then reached out to pull Mydei up with him in one cheerful motion.

“Let’s go,” he said brightly. “I’ll properly introduce you as my boyfriend to them too.”

Mydei nearly tripped over his own feet at that.

“Boy— what— Phainon,” he sputtered, heat shooting up his neck. “You can’t just say things like that so casually.”

Phainon only laughed, tightening his grip on Mydei’s waist before leaning in to give him a quick peck on the lips.

“Why not? It’s true,” he said simply. “And they’ll be thrilled. They’ve been suspicious for years.”

Mydei stared at him, the words taking a moment to sink in. 

“Suspicious of what?”

“That I was in love with you,” Phainon replied brightly.

Mydei’s mouth opened, closed, then opened again, but not a single word came out.

Phainon just grinned wider and tugged him forward by the hand.

“Come on. The sooner we go, the sooner my mother will cry, hug both of us, and probably feed you too much of her cooking.”

They walked side by side toward the village, Phainon humming something cheerful under his breath while Mydei tried very hard not to trip over his own thoughts. The closer they got, the more Mydei’s nerves tightened in his chest.

When they reached Phainon’s home, the small cottage looked just as welcoming as always. Smoke curled lazily from the chimney, and the smell of cooking drifted through the air, comforting in a way that made Mydei’s nerves flutter even more.

Phainon only grinned and pushed the door open.

“Mother! Father! I brought my boyfriend!”

Mydei nearly choked on air.

Inside, Phainon’s mother dropped the wooden spoon she was holding. His father froze mid-swing with the bundle of wheat he was sorting. Both of them snapped their heads toward the doorway and simply gaped.

Meanwhile, Phainon just stood there beaming.

“Y-Your Highness,” his father said, still visibly startled as he stepped forward. “This is… quite an unexpected honor.”

Mydei straightened instinctively as the old habit of royal decorum settled over him. Though inside, he wanted nothing more than to sink into the ground and disappear.

“You don’t need to be formal with me,” he said quickly, giving a small bow of his head. “I came to apologize for what happened last night. The royal guards acted under a misunderstanding.”

Phainon’s mother finally snapped out of her shock and hurried forward, fussing over Mydei instead.

“Oh heavens, you shouldn’t be apologizing to us! Come inside, come inside!” she said, ushering him in like he was a stray kitten she’d suddenly decided to adopt. “Have you eaten? Are you hungry? Sit, sit!”

Mydei barely had time to blink before he was seated at the small wooden table, the warm smell of home-cooked food all around him.

Meanwhile, Phainon still stood in the doorway, watching Mydei grow more overwhelmed by the second, grinning like this was the best day of his life.

“Mydei,” his mother said, already reaching for a pot on the stove, “you must try this soup. It’s fresh. Oh, and bread—Phainon, get the bread. Don’t just stand there smiling like that.”

Phainon finally stepped inside. “Yes, Mother,” he said lightly. He then set the fresh loaf of bread on the table and took the seat right beside Mydei, close enough that their shoulders brushed. Mydei tried not to look as flustered as he felt.

Phainon’s mother ladled steaming soup into a bowl and placed it in front of him with a proud smile.

“There. Try it while it’s hot.”

Mydei murmured a soft thanks and lifted the spoon. The first taste was warm, rich, and surprisingly delicious. His eyes widened before he could stop himself.
